content.text: An alternative to DBXML (and to a memory-based or simple file-based policy indexing/caching mechanism) could be exist -
http://exist.sourceforge.net
Benefits over DBXML
written in Java
deployable either as a servlet in the same container as Fedora, or separate (comes with Jetty to do this)
It is LGPL, therefore there should be no licensing issues distributing with Fedora and linking to it.

I'm not sure where thinking now is on this issue, but I'd like to +1 Steve's suggestion of eXist. It's a strong product that could be integrated either as Steve imagines or as an internal dependency inside Fedora, for an even smaller install footprint. Of course, it is nice to be able to separate the policy store fro the main webapp, as well.

Other options could be BaseX[1] or Qizx [2], or Qizx/open [3] with something behind it.  The requirements are fairly low, we just need to provide indexed-access to policies based on certain policy elements.  Other suggestions, experiences, welcomed!
http://www.inf.uni-konstanz.de/dbis/basex/
http://www.xmlmind.com/qizx/
http://www.xmlmind.com/qizxopen/

Regarding eXist DB, which is integrated within Orbeon xforms engine. I'd like to say it might not be as stable as you expect. In our system, it crashed a few times and made orbeon stopping working. We didn't investigate whether it's an issue with Orbeon or with eXist itself.

Another point: it would be well to choose a database offering some common (Java) API to provide for migration from one store to another as users find that appropriate. I suspect that XQJ might be the right API to which to program. XML:DB is another candidate. Of course, support for these APIs varies from product to product.

We should also consider a non XML database option.  The XPath queries to be executed are not free-form, and are well-known (selecting a set of policies based on an essentially fixed set of XACML values).  We could potentially move to a higher-level abstraction, ie the interface doesn't receive XPath queries but a data structure specifying the XACML values (and beneath this, where the implementation is an XML database, the XPath queries would get built).
So, index up front (in memory, SQL, etc) based on the known locations of the XACML values that will be searched upon.
I think it might be worth re factoring the code to use Xaj - "a small Java API for accessing XML-enabled databases" - it support Berkeley DB XML, Exist, DB2 et al.
http://xaj.sourceforge.net/
It also seems to support deadlock detection for DB XML, which can cause corruptions in the database if not properly handled, as raised in the related JIRA - 846
https://jira.duraspace.org/browse/FCREPO-846
Thanks Nigel, I will take a look at xaj
As part of this issue:
refactor the PolicyIndex API - there are many unused methods.  Review the methods actually needed that are relevant to a policy cache (rather than necessarily a full ACID transactional database).
review the locking/read-error code in the DBXML policy index to see if we can come up with a generic solution if appropriate
review where validation takes place (see also
) - this should be at a higher level than the policy index (and we should also check for well-formed-ness)

Part 1: Simple in-memory PolicyIndex added.  This maintains a local cache directory of policies which is cached in memory when the server starts.  The index does not in fact do any indexing - queries for matching policies will return all policies for evaluation (similar to what the legacy XACML implementation does).  Probably suitable where there is a small number of policies.  Could be enhanced to do indexing.
Adding eXist support requires adding the XML:DB API to the distribution.  xmldb.jar added to local repo, this needs adding to a maven repo.  Currently added to pom as xmldb/xmldb-api/1.4
Source of this is from the eXist software distribution (but covered by XML:DB licence).  XML:DB API licence added to Fedora licence directory.
eXist client files required (to make the XML:DB API work) are (from eXist distribution)
exist.jar (contains more than client classes, but there is no separate client jar)
xmlrpc-client-3.1.2.jar
xmlrpc-common-3.1.2.jar
ws-commons-utils-1.0.2.jar
Setup instructions need to reflect this (ie adding the above to the classpath, either Fedora's lib or some common location)
Merged into master

This has been discussed before, just making a note of it here. This should go hand-in-hand with the move to make policies first-class objects in the Fedora repository. Ideally, we'd give the repository manager the option to cache policies in memory or use dbxml for repositories with a lot of policies.
